title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
gist: Teaser of a subscriber-only OnPoint piece: Jayant Sinha argues that US-China dominance over every layer of the AI stack threatens to reproduce colonial dynamics, and middle powers must jointly build an open AI stack with common governance standards.

insights.claim: The United States and China control virtually every layer of the AI stack—hardware, data systems, software, and apps—entering the AI age with clear technological dominance over all other countries.
insights.speaker: JAYANT SINHA
insights.so_what: Value capture in AI is concentrated in two jurisdictions; others face dependency.
insights.quote: These two superpowers now control virtually every layer of the “stack”: the hardware, data systems, software, and apps that, together, compose AI.

insights.claim: The US and China are investing in AI infrastructure at a pace other countries cannot match, according to Jayant Sinha.
insights.speaker: JAYANT SINHA
insights.so_what: The capex gap entrenches the duopoly and creates demand for sovereign-AI alternatives.
insights.quote: They are also investing in AI infrastructure at a pace other countries cannot match.

insights.claim: Sinha warns the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution, producing digital colonization of countries outside the US and China.
insights.speaker: JAYANT SINHA
insights.so_what: Expect policy pushback (data localization, sovereign AI) from middle powers like India.
insights.quote: the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution
insights.locator: As the United States and China

insights.claim: To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.
insights.speaker: JAYANT SINHA
insights.so_what: Watch for multilateral open-source AI and sovereign-compute initiatives among middle powers as investment opportunities.
